Chapter 6. The Ripple Effects of Past Decisions
Have you ever noticed how a choice made in just a single afternoon can echo for years—or even decades? In business, the past is never really gone. It sticks around in contracts, in the way teams interact, in the stories people tell about what worked and what didn’t.
Let’s take a look at a few stories that bring this to life—not with rose-colored glasses, but with a clear sense of how the decisions we make yesterday shape what we’re dealing with today.
Picture this: there’s a certain kind of meeting that feels heavy even before it starts. In one of these rooms, a group of executives sits around a glossy table, looking back at the legacy of a merger that happened years ago. At the time, that deal seemed like a stroke of genius—two strong companies joining forces to take on the world.
But as time passed, the cracks started to show. Systems didn’t fit together the way people hoped. Cultures clashed. And those famous “synergies” never really came to life.
One manager, who joined just after the merger, found herself constantly caught in the middle of old rivalries. Even little things—like choosing which team would lead a project—were tangled up in memories of who “won” or “lost” during the original deal. It turned out that the merger wasn’t just about numbers on a page. It became a story people told themselves—about who they were, and where they belonged.
Now, in another corner of the business world, a family-owned company was facing a different kind of challenge. Decades before, the founder had promised to keep the business in the family, no matter what. But now, with a new generation stepping up, that promise started to feel less like a gift and more like a heavy weight.
Siblings found themselves arguing over which direction to take. Employees worried about what the future would look like. And the founder watched, feeling both proud and a little regretful.
Here’s something to pay attention to: in both of these stories, the lesson is the same. Decisions made in the heat of the moment can cast long shadows. Most of us don’t realize just how much our present is shaped by the stories and promises of the past.
It’s so easy to forget that every decision—whether it’s bold or careful, generous or just looking out for yourself—sets a path that others will have to walk.
And the ripple effects of those choices? They’re almost never obvious right away. You’ll see them later, in the way people trust—or maybe don’t trust—each other. In how willing folks are to take chances. In the stories that get told in break rooms and boardrooms alike.
Over time, you start to see that the real legacy of any decision isn’t just what gets accomplished, but how it changes the people who live with the consequences.
